title: Quantum Vacuum Nonlinearities in Laser Interferometers
authors: Zain Mehdi, Joseph J. Hope, Simon A. Haine
abstract: We propose all-optical tests of photon-photon interactions in the matter vacuum using standing-wave laser interferometers, which do not require external magnetic fields and use conventional laser sources. We show that the interferometric detection of photon-photon scattering predicted by quantum electrodynamics is within reach of laboratory-scale experiments with a sensitivity that improves nonlinearly with the circulating power within the cavity. We outline how such an experiment could be adapted to probe properties of quantum fields beyond the Standard Model of particle physics.
summary: This paper outlines a method to experimentally test the nonlinear interaction between photons in the vacuum using high-finesse laser interferometers. By analyzing the effective Hamiltonian derived from QED, the authors predict a measurable phase shift proportional to the optical power. The work details the necessary quantum estimation techniques to determine the sensitivity and feasibility of such a measurement.
main_problem: The paper proposes all-optical methods to test photon-photon interactions in the vacuum, which are predicted by Quantum Electrodynamics (QED). It aims to do this without requiring external magnetic fields.
main_result: The measurable signal is a phase shift ($\phi$) or a differential phase shift ($\delta$) in a standing-wave laser interferometer, which scales nonlinearly with the circulating optical power.
method: The analysis involves deriving effective interaction Hamiltonians ($\hat{H}_{	ext{SM}}$ and $\hat{H}_{	ext{TM}}$) from the Euler-Heisenberg effective action and calculating the resulting phase shifts and achievable Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR) using quantum estimation theory.
model_or_system: The system is a standing-wave laser interferometer utilizing a Fabry-Perot cavity. The underlying physics is the nonlinear interaction between photons mediated by vacuum zero-point fluctuations, described by QED effective Lagrangians.
key_observables: Phase shift ($\phi$), differential phase shift ($\delta$), and the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR).
important_parameters: Optical power ($P_0$), cavity volume ($V$), vacuum susceptibility parameters ($\alpha^2$), and the cavity finesse ($F$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the rotating-wave approximation (RWA) and assumes the detection is shot-noise limited, with some advanced sections considering squeezed light states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the general QED interaction Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{	ext{int}}$) to specific single-mode ($\hat{H}_{	ext{SM}}$) and two-mode ($\hat{H}_{	ext{TM}}$) interactions. It then calculates the resulting phase shifts and finally analyzes the achievable precision limits using quantum estimation theory (QFI).
why_interesting: This work directly bridges high-energy physics predictions (QED vacuum effects) with cutting-edge experimental quantum optics techniques (interferometry and quantum metrology), making it highly relevant for AMO physicists working on quantum field measurements.
